newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ethnic Chinese to face trial over Indonesia riot.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic Chinese to face trial over Indonesia riot.

text.p: An Indonesian man of Chinese descent will be tried over a riot he is accused of inciting in West Java in January during which churches and Chinese temples were attacked, the Republika newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted West Java Police Chief Major-General Nana Permana as saying on Tuesday that the man, identified as Kim Tjay, would be tried soon on charges of insult.
"The suspect will be charged with commiting verbal assault," Permana said without elaborating.
Kim's wife, Giok, has also been accused of inciting the riot in Rengasdengklok, 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta. Giok was arrested after the riot but it was unclear when she would be tried.

Government officials said the riot apparently started after Giok complained of the noise Moslem youths were making as they beat drums before dawn summoning people to eat before the start of daytime fasting during the month of Ramadan.
Republika said Kim later threw stones to the small mosque, located beside his house, where the youths beat the drum.
The mainly Moslem mob attacked churches and Chinese temples during the riot and looted homes and shops. Sixteen cars were also burned.
Meanwhile, 18 Indonesians will be tried for taking part in riots in late December in West Kalimantan province bordering Malaysia's Sarawak state.
A fight over a girl sparked the violence between native Dayaks and migrants from Madura island.
